presentingComplaint: Constant right upper quadrant pain for 18 hours with fever and vomiting
history: Obese multiparous woman with known gallstones on prior ultrasound. Episodic post-prandial RUQ colic for months, but this episode began after a fatty meal and has persisted continuously for ~18 hours (unlike her usual self-limiting colic). Pain radiates to the right scapular tip, associated with anorexia, nausea and two episodes of vomiting. Low-grade fever with rigors overnight. No dark urine, no pale stools, no confusion. PMH: type 2 diabetes, dyslipidaemia. No prior biliary surgery. No recent travel.
examination: Ill-appearing, febrile. Marked RUQ tenderness with guarding; inspiratory arrest on deep palpation of the RUQ (positive Murphy sign). No palpable gallbladder mass. Sclerae anicteric. Bowel sounds present, no peritonism elsewhere. No stigmata of chronic liver disease; no asterixis.
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound: distended gallbladder with wall thickening (5 mm), pericholecystic fluid, multiple echogenic gallstones with acoustic shadowing, and a sonographic Murphy sign. Common bile duct not dilated (4 mm). No intrahepatic biliary dilatation.
microbiology: Blood cultures drawn, pending. (If cholecystectomy performed, bile cultures commonly grow E. coli, Klebsiella or Enterococcus.)
citations: Harrison 22e — Diseases of the Gallbladder and Bile Ducts
stewardship: Community-acquired, non-severe (Grade I-II) acute cholecystitis: empiric IV cefuroxime plus metronidazole (or ceftriaxone + metronidazole) to cover enteric Gram-negatives and anaerobes, alongside analgesia, IV fluids and early laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Rationale: coverage targets gut flora (E. coli, Klebsiella, Enterococcus, Bacteroides) that seed obstructed bile; source control is definitive.
contraindications: Avoid nephrotoxic aminoglycosides given diabetic nephropathy risk; adjust for eGFR
edgeCases: Acalculous cholecystitis in critically ill/fasting/diabetic patients — no stones on US but wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid
Mirizzi syndrome or evolving choledocholithiasis if bilirubin/ALP rise — reassess for cholangitis and consider MRCP/ERCP
Emphysematous cholecystitis (gas in gallbladder wall) in diabetics — surgical emergency
expectedMaiK: Continuous RUQ pain >6h with positive Murphy sign, fever, neutrophilia and ultrasound gallstones plus a thickened gallbladder wall indicate acute calculous cholecystitis rather than simple biliary colic; near-normal bilirubin and a non-dilated CBD argue against concurrent cholangitis, but rising bilirubin should prompt reassessment.
expectedNextQuestions: Is the pain now continuous and lasting more than 6 hours (versus self-limiting colic)?
Any jaundice, dark urine, or rigors suggesting duct obstruction/cholangitis?
expectedInvestigations: LFTs and lipase to exclude cholangitis/pancreatitis
HIDA scan or MRCP if ultrasound equivocal
regressionAssertions: differential must include CHOLANGITIS and biliary_colic
must not down-rank to pure biliary_colic given positive Murphy sign + fever + leukocytosis
